verdict.rationale: v0's own GitHub integration keeps project code in a repository with branches and pull requests, and offers Import from GitHub, so a developer can edit the repo locally and bring that code into v0. The docs never describe a round-trip where local commits pushed to the connected repo sync back into the existing v0 chat or project, nor any local CLI or editor workflow. missing for 10: documented two-way sync of locally pushed changes into an existing v0 project, explicit local-editor or CLI workflow docs, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can work on the app locally with my own editor and tooling and push changes back to the platform

citations.quote: Connect a v0 project to GitHub to keep its code in a repository, work on isolated branches, preview changes, run CI, and publish through pull requests.
To start from code already on GitHub, use Import from GitHub. Importing creates a chat at the selected base branch
Connect to GitHub and push code directly to your repository.
